pull.title: KAFKA-21370: Return STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH for topology epoch mismatches
pull.body:
KIP-1071 defines STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH for a member that sends
a topology that differs from the group's topology at the same epoch, but
the group coordinator returned INVALID_REQUEST in that case. The streams
group heartbeat now returns STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH when the
topology differs at the same epoch. When the topology differs at a
higher epoch, it keeps returning INVALID_REQUEST, since topology updates
are not supported yet.

The KIP-1331 topology description push also returns
STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH instead of INVALID_REQUEST when the
pushed epoch does not match the group's current topology epoch, and
StreamsGroupTopologyDescriptionUpdateResponse lists it as a supported
error. Client behavior does not change. The heartbeat request manager
already treats STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH as fatal, the same as
INVALID_REQUEST, and the topology description request manager now names
it explicitly among the errors that drop the push without retrying.

Reviewers: ChickenchickenLove <ojt90902@naver.com>

review_comments.body: This is technically a KIP change, but more of a bug fix. There is no difference in how the clients treats this error, it's just more specific on the wire. I'd just amend KIP-1331 for this.
SGTM. -- Can we backport this to 4.4.1 ? Do we need to document it explicitly on the webpage (I would think no, but just wanted to double check).

nit;

review_comments.body: I'm not sure the split buys us much here. The push carries a TopologyDescription, not the heartbeat Topology, so at the same epoch there's nothing to compare it against. A member with a different topology at the same epoch already gets STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH on the heartbeat and fails before it pushes. For a stale push, returning NONE without storing it would be misleading, and the client clears the push flag on either result anyway. Also, since topology updates aren't supported, the group's topology epoch doesn't move after initialization, so a mismatch here means a buggy client or a recreated group. I'd keep a single error for now and revisit when topology updates land. WDYT?
Done, added it to that list.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21370: Return STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH for topology epoch mismatches

KIP-1071 defines STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH for a member that sends a
topology that differs from the group's topology at the same epoch, but the
group coordinator returned INVALID_REQUEST in that case. The streams group
heartbeat now returns STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH when the topology differs
at the same epoch, and keeps INVALID_REQUEST when the topology differs at a
higher epoch, since topology updates are not supported.

The KIP-1331 topology description push also returns
STREAMS_INVALID_TOPOLOGY_EPOCH instead of INVALID_REQUEST when the pushed
epoch does not match the group's current topology epoch. The client handles
it like before, dropping the push without retrying, but logs it at info level,
since the epoch can change between the heartbeat that requested the push and
the push itself.
